question: Can a continuous epsilon-anchored min-max RGB coordinate retain the characteristic shape while jointly preserving cube boundaries, channel order and photographic gradients?

operator.anchored_curve: identity outside [epsilon,1-epsilon]; inside, normalize to [0,1], apply the exact CB8 convex characteristic curve, then denormalize
operator.minmax_coordinate: use ordered knots at the per-pixel min, epsilon, 1-epsilon and max when present; boundary segments remain identity, while channels in the interior preserve normalized position between the clipped min/max interior knots after those endpoints are mapped
operator.contracts: continuous, symmetric in channel labels, channel-order preserving, neutral preserving, cube bounded and no new epsilon boundary
operator.forbidden: hard clipping, per-pixel alpha minimum, spatial smoothing, curve refit or strength rescue

stop_rules: Do not change curve, strength, epsilon, coordinate, population, controls or gates after candidate pixels are scored.
Any automatic failure closes this exact coordinate before visual review and without rescue.
Pass opens severe visual review only; it does not establish Velvia calibration, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
claim_ceiling: Rights-cleared photographic development evidence for a continuous intrinsic RGB coordinate compiled from a retained reversal characteristic shape; not Velvia calibration, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
